scope_note: EN-16 is a large (L) item. This slice delivers the kernel-BPF map memory ledger and utilization-pressure hysteresis, verified end to end. Remaining gaps are listed in report.md.
deliverables: kernel_bpf_budget_bytes added to GovernorSnapshot (bounded by the node state budget; cgroup-aware)
bpf_map_specs() extracted as the single source of map truth (31 maps, in sync with all #[map] declarations)
projected_bpf_map_bytes(): worst-case pinned kernel memory per map type — hash +64B/entry, per-CPU maps x nr_cpus, LPM trie lazy-but-bounded, array/prog-array/xsk +8B/entry
ensure_bpf_map_budget(): pre-load attach gate — over-budget objects refuse attach explicitly (no silent pinning of unaccounted kernel memory)
audit_loaded_map_specs(): post-load audit — every map the object declares must match a spec-table entry (name + type + sizes), otherwise attach fails naming the offending map
utilization-driven L4 pressure hysteresis: entry bands 70/85/95, exit bands 60/75/90 — boundary workloads hold their level instead of flapping protective behaviour
unit tests: projection boundedness, budget bounded by state budget, hysteresis enter/exit semantics

verification.environment: OrbStack x86 VM, kernel 7.0.14-orbstack, cgroup v2
verification.unit: xdp 78 tests + l4_defense 38 tests pass on macOS host build; Linux lib builds clean on x86-build

probe_results.A_ledger_observable: projectedBytes=382756816 (~365 MiB) <= budgetBytes=412300738 on unconstrained host; matches measured bpftool memlock ~365 MB within model error
probe_results.B_positive_attach: node attaches XDP under the normal budget
probe_results.C_budget_refusal: under cgroup memory.max=4GiB the budget shrinks to ~341 MiB < 382.7 MiB projection; node exits with explicit error 'eBPF map projected memory 382756816 exceeds kernel-bpf budget 342530457'; no link pin created

verification.regression: EN-09 pending probe re-run on the gated attach path: all 5 phases pass (one earlier run flaked during topology setup; rerun green)
audit_existing_coverage: RAII permits (AdmissionPermit/ZeroCopyRelayPermit/UdpQueueBytePermit/ActiveIpPermit) release on Drop — cancellation/timeout cannot leak permits
AF_XDP UMEM projection sums all queues against one node budget — queues cannot each claim a full node budget
logical admission accounting is derived-from but not charged-against physical RSS/cgroup observation — no double counting

limitations: per-listener/per-service quota pools are not yet enforced — ServiceIdentity exists as a contract; unknown-tenant traffic is admitted to the node-level pool, not a listener-scoped pool
the map projection is a model (calibrated within ~10% of measured memlock on kernel 7.0), not an exact kernel accounting; the post-load spec audit prevents silent drift between object and ledger
hysteresis applies to the utilization channel (connection/fd/quic pcts); memory-level, aggregate-surge and syn-defense channels escalate and clear immediately
no disk/spool ledger — node-local disk writers (logs, cache) keep their existing configured bounds outside the governor
